Subject: Perturb Labs — Mutual Success Checklist & Lane Assignments (POC)

Hi Tom / Perturb team,

Thanks again for your time today — good alignment on goals. Below is a concise post-call recap, a proposed evaluation plan, and a simple lane-assignment so we can move to a hands-on POC quickly.

A. Primary success criteria (what success looks like)
- End-to-end median generation latency <= 220ms (95th <= 600ms) under a 1 RPS realistic user mix
- Sustained throughput target: 50 qps with batching enabled (representative prompt mix)
- Quality: your internal eval set shows >= 85% top-3 relevance match
- Observability: per-request traces + 30-day audit log availability

B. Proposed evaluation plan (4-week cadence)
- Week 1: network & credentials, test dataset ingest, and baseline inference run
- Week 2: tune batching/KV cache, inflection tests on sequence lengths
- Week 3: load tests (50 qps), latency/throughput reporting, quality evals
- Week 4: review runbook, findings, and go/no-go decision

C. Lane assignments (RACI-lite; please confirm):
- Perturb app owner: Tom Ellis (Perturb)
- Perturb infra lead: (please confirm infra contact)
- Redwood deployment lead: Ben Carter
- Redwood infra engineer: Marcus Lin
- Security & controls (Perturb): Perturb Labs Security (cc'd)
- Procurement / billing contact: TBD (please confirm)

D. Initial asks from Perturb to enable the run:
- Confirm internal owners for infra, app, security, and procurement by Fri 2026-02-20
- Share a representative prompt set (10–20 prompts) and an estimated QPS distribution

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx, security-questionnaire-answers.pdf (see stubs below).

Next steps (proposed)
- Tom: confirm owners + procurement contact
- Redwood: provision trial pool once owners confirmed and share test harness + ingestion guide
- Schedule 30–45 minute kickoff the week after owners are confirmed

I'll follow up with a calendar invite after we have the owners.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Tom — looping in the infra/ops owners from Redwood to confirm how we'll run the POC and map responsibilities.

Short answers to the asks:
- Cold-starts: we will include a dedicated cold-start test in Week 2; expected median cold-start for a warmed pool is ~350–450ms; cold-start for a scaled-up container can be ~800–1200ms depending on model and GPU type. We'll run measurements and include them in the Week 2 report.

- Retention: we support 30d out of the box; 90d is possible via extended log retention (we'll include a cost estimate in the kickoff doc).

Proposed lane/RACI text (for confirmation):
- R: Perturb app owner (Tom Ellis) — define success metrics, provide prompt set and acceptance evals
- A: Redwood deployment lead (Ben Carter) — provision trial pool, manage model variants, run load tests
- C: Redwood infra engineer (Marcus Lin) — network setup, KV cache tuning, telemetry hooks
- I: Perturb Security (Laura Chen) — review questionnaire and sign-off on controls

Operational notes:
- We can provision a dedicated trial GPU pool and a sandbox VPC; earliest practical start is week of 2026-03-02 pending network/credentials and procurement sign-off.
- Action for Ben: prepare a short runbook (10–12 steps) for environment access and test harness by 2026-02-26.
